summary: Shell-script fix tested per request. Ran /app/tests/gdrive_backup_sim.sh in ok and mysqlfail modes, confirmed regression by swapping in the pre-fix version from git (commit 2e57fc8), ran `bash -n` on both scripts, and reviewed bash logic. All three required scenarios pass. Fix is correct and the user's reported bug is reproduced on the old version. No app code touched.
critical_code_review_comments: deploy/backup.sh line 8: MYSQL_PWD is set inside the inner sh -c before `exec mysqldump`, so password never appears on cmdline nor in docker's visible argv. Verified by sim harness: PASSWORD_ON_CMDLINE=0. The `[Warning] Using a password on the command line` user saw is gone.
deploy/backup.sh line 9: empty-dump check (`gzip -dc ... | head -c 1 | wc -c`) correctly catches zero-byte dumps; combined with `set -o pipefail` any mysqldump failure also propagates.

deploy/gdrive-backup.sh lines 34-37: Capturing full backup.sh output into RESULT and extracting with `sed -n 's#^Backup tersimpan di deploy/##p' | tail -1` is robust against the earlier double-prefix bug (`backups/backups/<ts>`). Also validates with `[ -d "$OUT" ]` and preserves original output in the error log for easier debugging.

Cron install (lines 11-20): TZ offset arithmetic (`SIGN`, 10# base, modulo wrap) correctly produces 17:00 UTC = 00:00 WIB. `grep -v 'gdrive-backup.sh'` cleanly replaces any previous cron line. No `set -e` pitfalls here.
env_value function (line 22): simple grep/cut/sed strips surrounding quotes; combined with `|| true` plays well with `set -u`. Suggest nothing; works as intended.

RCLONE array construction (45-55): safe quoting, mutually-exclusive token-vs-SA branch, SHARED_DRIVE optional. Minor nit (not a bug): script runs `docker run rclone/rclone sync /data gdrive:` with `--drive-use-trash=false` which permanently deletes prior Drive content on every run — this is the documented intent, worth keeping in mind for recovery.
seed_data_creation: None (sim harness creates its own temp workdir with fake docker binary and .env)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test harness lives at /app/tests/gdrive_backup_sim.sh. Modes: `ok` (happy path, expect exit 0, UPLOADED=crm-maiharta-backup-*.tar, 5 local files incl env.txt, PASSWORD_ON_CMDLINE=0) and `mysqlfail` (expect exit 1 with 'backup.sh gagal (lihat pesan error di atas)' + mysqldump error on stderr, UPLOADED empty). Note harness has a cosmetic quirk: its final `grep -c ... | sed` returns exit 1 under pipefail when 0 matches, so the surrounding `bash sim.sh; echo $?` prints 1, but that is AFTER 'EXIT=0' from the real script run — read EXIT= line, not harness $?. To reproduce the original user bug: `git show 2e57fc8:deploy/gdrive-backup.sh > deploy/gdrive-backup.sh; git show 2e57fc8:deploy/backup.sh > deploy/backup.sh` then run sim; restore from backup copies.

rca of the issue: Original bug: backup.sh echoed `Backup tersimpan di deploy/backups/<ts>`; gdrive-backup.sh used `OUT="backups/$(bash backup.sh | sed -n 's#^Backup tersimpan di deploy/##p')"` which stripped `deploy/` but then re-prefixed `backups/`, yielding `backups/backups/<ts>` — a non-existent path — triggering the `[ -d "$OUT" ]` failure branch and misleading 'backup.sh gagal'. Secondary issue: mysqldump invoked with `-p"$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD"` leaked the password onto the process cmdline (visible in `ps`/docker ps) and emitted the `[Warning] Using a password on the command line interface can be insecure` on stderr. Fix captures backup.sh output verbatim, extracts the path directly without re-prefixing, surfaces real errors with 'lihat pesan error di atas', and switches to `MYSQL_PWD` env (set inside `sh -c` before `exec mysqldump`) plus an empty-dump sanity check.
